output.hook: Figma hands engineers a pile of absolutely-positioned rectangles. gridframe hands them CSS Grid that actually works.

scenes.visual: Screen recording: a Figma inspect panel showing a component with 'position: absolute; left: 240px; top: 128px' — the classic handoff nightmare
scenes.voiceover: Every Figma handoff looks like this. Absolute positions. Magic numbers. Engineers rebuild the whole layout from scratch.

scenes.visual: gridframe canvas: designer sketching rough frame boxes — loose, imprecise strokes resolving in real time into a structured grid overlay with column and row guides snapping into place
scenes.voiceover: gridframe starts with structure, not rectangles. Sketch a rough frame and it resolves into a real responsive grid system — breakpoints included.

scenes.visual: Split screen: left side shows the gridframe layout audit panel lighting up with flagged overflow and breakpoint issues; right side shows a count badge reading '140 bugs caught'
scenes.voiceover: Before you even hand off, the layout audit runs. In alpha, it caught 140 overflow bugs across real production sites. Bugs that would've lived in the sprint backlog for weeks.

scenes.visual: gridframe export panel: clicking 'Export CSS' — then a code editor showing clean CSS Grid and Flexbox output, no absolute positioning, stylelint running and returning zero warnings
scenes.voiceover: Hit export. You get clean CSS Grid and Flexbox — zero absolute positioning, zero stylelint warnings. Code engineers will actually keep.

scenes.visual: Waitlist landing page at {APP_URL} with the headline and a simple email signup field
scenes.voiceover: 3,400 designers are already on the waitlist. If layout handoff is eating your sprints, come join them.

scenes.visual: gridframe wordmark on a clean background with {APP_URL} beneath it
scenes.voiceover: gridframe. Layouts that ship, not rectangles that lie.

production_notes: Capture a real Figma inspect panel showing absolute-position values on a multi-column component — do not mock this up, authenticity matters to the design-engineer audience
Record the gridframe canvas live: rough sketch strokes resolving into a grid system with visible breakpoint markers — this is the core 'aha' moment and needs to be smooth
Record the layout audit panel in action, ideally on a real alpha user's design file showing multiple flagged issues; the '140 bugs' stat must come from the on-screen count, not just voiceover
Record the CSS export flow end-to-end: export click → code output in a real editor (VS Code preferred) → stylelint terminal run returning zero warnings — do not cut before the terminal result appears
Capture the waitlist page at {APP_URL} with a real browser address bar visible — builds trust that the product exists
Keep all recordings at 1x zoom or slightly zoomed in — no tiny UI that viewers can't read on mobile
No background music that competes with voiceover; subtle ambient or silence preferred given the quality-obsessed brand voice
warnings: No public demo or sandbox exists yet — do not promise or imply viewers can try the product immediately; the CTA correctly directs to the waitlist only
The '140 overflow bugs' proof point is self-reported from alpha users — do not add any qualifier beyond what the profile states, but avoid framing it as an independent benchmark
The '3,400 waitlist signups' figure is pre-launch and self-reported — use it as social proof but do not imply it represents paying customers or active users
No Figma import integration exists yet — do not show or imply any Figma file import flow in the canvas recording
